rationale: No suitable optimization is supported for this workflow with its prerequisites met. The workflow already applies dependency caching (CPM packages and pandoc caches, matching P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) and run superseding via concurrency with cancel-in-progress: true (matching P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE). Patterns that do not fit: P-LIT-FAIL-FAST requires a matrix (single job only); schedule-based patterns (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE) require a schedule trigger (none present); Bazel patterns (P-LIT-BAZEL-*) require Bazel (workflow uses cmake/meson); P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST requires multiple jobs (single job). P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is the closest candidate, but its precondition is representative successful-duration history, and the repository context explicitly reports ci_history measurement as not_a_measured_baseline with no run durations. Setting an arbitrary timeout risks the documented contraindication that valid slow runs exceed the limit, especially since this job builds many C++ targets with both clang and gcc plus meson, which could easily exceed a conservative limit. Therefore no change is proposed.
